title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in these notes for the 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex, Grothendieck builds a dictionary between mod-2-graded coalgebras M over O_X (or over k) and their 'generic algebra' V(M), the functor A ↦ Hom(M, A) with the convolution product. On the previous page, M is called anticommutative (resp. alternating) when V(M) is. This page carries the dictionary over to derivations.

(1) Coderivations and anti-coderivations. He defines k-coderivations of a coalgebra, and k-anti-coderivations: odd endomorphisms of M, i.e. those exchanging the parities of degrees. They are defined as exactly the endomorphisms that dualize to derivations, resp. antiderivations, of the mod-2-graded O_X-algebra V(M).

(2) Bracket stability. From that definition he reads off stability under brackets. In modern terms, the derivations together with the antiderivations form a Lie superalgebra under the graded commutator.
- The commutator of two derivations is a derivation.
- The anticommutator of two odd antiderivations is an even derivation.
- The commutator of a derivation with an antiderivation is an antiderivation.
The same therefore holds for coderivations.

(3) Degree conventions. If M is Z-graded and an endomorphism of M has degree i, the induced endomorphism of V(M) has degree −i. This is the usual reversal under dualization. It can be avoided by re-indexing with the trick V(M)_i = V(M)^i = V(M^{-i}). For questions of derivations versus antiderivations only the degree mod 2 matters, and the parity of i equals that of −i, so no distinction is needed.

(4) Programme. One treats analogously comodules, co-derivations and divided-power ('à puissances divisées') structures on a coalgebra. To do this in the right generality — not only the commutative case but also the anticommutative/alternating case needed for de Rham complexes — one must first have the notions in the ordinary (non-'co') algebra case. That means divided-power structures on alternating graded algebras, in Roby's style. These are then transported to coalgebras through V.

(5) Next page. The following page starts this foundational work: general facts on coalgebras and comodules, recovering a comodule structure from the module structure over the dual algebra S^k after all base changes.
errors: If the line reads 'l'anti-crochet de deux antidérivations est une antidérivation', it is wrong as stated. The anticommutator of two odd antiderivations is an even derivation (cf. Cartan: dι + ιd = L). The image is ambiguous here (it may read 'produit/crochet' and the line break may hide 'dérivation'), so this is flagged only as a possible slip.
Strictly, 'product of two derivations is a derivation' must mean commutator (crochet); the literal composite of two derivations is not a derivation.

ideas.what: Describing a coalgebra M through its functor of points A ↦ Hom(M,A) (the generic algebra V(M)), and defining (anti)coderivations as endomorphisms dualizing to (anti)derivations of V(M)
ideas.modern_name: Convolution / dual algebra functor; coderivations of (super)coalgebras

ideas.what: Derivations and odd antiderivations of a mod-2-graded algebra are closed under graded commutators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Cartan; Frölicher–Nijenhuis; Kac 1977 for super terminology)

ideas.what: A degree-i endomorphism dualizes to degree −i; only parity matters for sign rules
ideas.modern_name: Grading reversal under duality; Koszul sign rule depends only on parity

ideas.what: Programme: define divided-power structures on alternating/anticommutative graded algebras first, then dualize to coalgebras and comodules via V
ideas.modern_name: Divided power (super)algebras and DP coalgebras; Roby's strictly anticommutative DP algebras

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine foundational bookkeeping: the super-sign conventions for (anti)coderivations via the dual-algebra functor and degree reversal. It sets up the divided-power coalgebra framework of the lecture, and all of it is standard in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'divisions'/'antidivisions' should read 'dérivations'/'antidérivations', matching the de Rham context and the preceding page's 'k-codérivations ... k-antidérivations'.
First line '→ M:ri[?] de degré impair' should be the tail of '(anti)dérivations de degré impair, i.e. échangeant parités des degrés'.
'le produit de deux divisions' is probably 'le crochet de deux dérivations'; 'l'anti-produit' is probably 'l'anti-crochet'.
'si $\mathcal{E}$ (vecteur[?] à une graduation[?] de degrés quelc.)' is probably 'si M (muni d'une graduation de degrés quelc.)'.
'est gradué[?] mod 2' is probably '(gr. mod 2)', i.e. V(M) considered as graded mod 2.
'coprincipaux[?] divisées' is probably 'co-puissances divisées' / 'coalgèbres à puissances divisées'.
'plus aussi le cas anti-commutatif' should be 'mais aussi le cas anti-commutatif'.
'dans le cas par "co", mais ordinaire' should be 'dans le cas pas "co", mais ordinaire'.
